briefs.headline: Trump vs Carney: Cars, homes, booze and more caught in US-Canada tariff war
briefs.deck: The recent imposition of new tariffs on vehicles and construction materials has intensified the trade conflict between the US and Canada. This has also led to surging import taxes on other household products and alcoholic beverages. Both businesses and consumers are likely to feel the pinch with escalating costs, potentially affecting employment rates. Moreover, these disputes cast a shadow of…
briefs.bodyText:
The US-Canada trade war has intensified, with both countries imposing fresh tariffs on a range of goods, including cars, building materials, household products and alcohol. The latest measures come after US President Donald Trump's threat to raise tariffs on Canadian imports, prompting Prime Minister Mark Carney's government to announce retaliatory duties on several US products.
The two North American neighbours have been locked in a bitter economic conflict since Trump returned to the White House and launched his flagship trade policy. While the tariffs could raise costs for businesses and consumers, the impact could also extend to jobs, investment and cross-border trade, with the USMCA trade agreement between the US, Canada and Mexico also facing greater uncertainty.
Cars face higher tariffs
Trump has threatened to raise tariffs on Canadian vehicles from 25% to 50% from January 1, 2027.
Cars, trucks and parts are among the main goods traded between the US, Canada and Mexico, with manufacturing and supply chains stretching across borders.
Previous tariffs have increased costs for manufacturers, but dealerships have absorbed the "lion's share", Bernard Yaros, lead economist at Oxford Economics told BBC.
"But that cushion is wearing thin," he adds. "The recently threatened 50% tariffs on Canadian autos, trucks, and car parts would feed through to consumer prices more readily than before."
Yaros said higher import costs could push manufacturers towards luxury cars, SUVs and pick-up trucks, while a shortage of cheaper new vehicles could raise used-car prices.
Carney has not matched Trump's 50% tariff threat, but Canada has had a 25% import tax on certain American vehicles since last year.
Building materials could raise housing costs
Steel, aluminium and lumber have already faced tariffs, while Canada has now matched US rates on metals at 50%.
Carney has also imposed import taxes on US wood products such as plywood and screws used to fix timber together.
Building firms could face higher costs and pass them on through higher prices, pushing up the cost of homes.
The Forest Products Association of Canada said tariffs would "raise costs on both sides of the border".
In the US, Bill Owens, chairman of the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB), urged Trump to exempt building materials because of an "ongoing housing affordability crisis".
"Building material tariffs heighten market uncertainty, strain supply chains and increase construction costs," he says.
The US imported $23 billion worth of wood products in 2024, with almost half coming from Canada, according to a US Congress report. Disputes over softwood lumber used in housebuilding stretch back decades.
Household goods also targeted
Canada has targeted carpets, washing machines, furniture, fridges, knives, forks and spoons.
Bradley Saunders, North America economist at Capital Economics, said consumers could instead turn to domestic alternatives.
He said Carney had targeted goods where Canadians could "shift to domestic suppliers instead".
"Like hair care products, you really can just buy that domestically instead," he adds, as cited by BBC.
Saunders said the move aimed to "minimise the impact on Canadian households as much as possible by picking very fungible goods".
The Budget Lab at Yale expects marginal increases in furnishing and other household equipment costs for Americans, mainly because of tariffs on lumber and other materials.
US alcohol sales face another hit
Several Canadian provinces banned US alcohol sales last year after earlier tariffs, while the American wine and spirits industry said exports to Canada fell by more than 70%.
Carney had asked provinces to restore US alcohol to their shelves during trade talks, but with talks collapsed, the ban is likely to return.
Saunders said politicians had pushed "buy Canadian", which had been successful for spirits.
"That's really had an impact on the American alcohol industry," he adds.
Saskatchewan and Alberta are the only provinces that still sell American alcohol. Saskatchewan has announced a 50% charge on US-imported alcohol from September 8, when the wider Canadian tariffs take effect.
Jobs and wider economy
Tariffs can also affect jobs. Businesses with cross-border supply chains face higher costs, while uncertainty could delay investment and limit job creation.
Saunders said job losses could have a bigger impact on households than higher prices.
"If you're, let's say, a bespoke furniture producer in BC [British Columbia], you're now facing a 50% tariff on your exports to the US - that could really shut the business down. I think that would be more the direct impact on households as opposed to these retaliatory measures."
Canada's forest industry employs almost 200,000 people and has urged the government to boost domestic demand through federal housing programmes to make greater use of Canadian wood. However, it said "no support package can replace reliable access to our largest export market".
For US consumers, the latest Canada dispute is unlikely to have a major impact on living costs. But trade tensions could create longer-term economic effects and uncertainty around the USMCA, the free-trade agreement between Canada, the US and Mexico.
Canada and Mexico want the USMCA extended for another 16 years, while the US has said it will not renew it in its current form. Although the deal remains operational, tariffs could put off talks.

briefs.headline: Nepal seeks to import power earlier from India after flood devastation, asks for approvals
briefs.deck: While the Himalayan country usually imports electricity from India during the winter months, it has now asked that the required approvals for sending power be processed in September itself
briefs.bodyText:
In the wake of the devastating flash flood that severely impacted Nepal’s power infrastructure, Kathmandu has asked India to give the requisite approvals for the transmission of electricity to Nepal earlier than usual, senior officials in the Union Power Ministry said on Saturday (August 29, 2026).
“Nepal has asked that India advance import approvals, starting from September this year, in view of the generation deficits caused by this disaster. The concerned authorities are processing the requests,” an official said. According to officials, India is willing to provide any additional power that Nepal may need.
Nepal usually imports electricity from India during the winter months, starting around October, as power generation is typically low in the Himalayan country during the freezing winter months. Conversely, the country exports its excess hydropower to India during the summer. According to official data, India imported 3,299 million units (MUs) of power from Nepal in fiscal year 2025-26 and exported 1,451 MUs to it.
Transmission of electricity across India’s borders requires mandatory clearances from the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), among others.
India ‘capable of absorbing shortfall’
According to an internal assessment, Nepal’s electricity generation capacity has declined by about 550 megawatts because of the infrastructural damage induced by the flood.
Officials said that this resulted in the cross-border power flow to India reducing by approximately 400 MW from earlier peaks of 950 MW to 1,000 MW. However, the officials assured that India was not foreseeing any requirement to make alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortfall.
“We do not foresee any requirement for exceptional emergency procurement or alternative arrangement to balance domestic demand,” an official said, adding, “India’s vast national grid capacity and robust generation reserve margins are capable of absorbing a temporary shortfall of 400 MW seamlessly without disrupting grid stability or retail supply."
The flash flood in the Nepal-Tibet border regions has killed about 675 people, authorities in Nepal said on Saturday. The country’s meteorology department has, meanwhile, warned of fresh rainfall and thunderstorms in the affected areas.

briefs.headline: IRDAI panel calls for simpler, transparent, easier-to-use health covers
briefs.bodyText:
A sub-committee on health insurance headed by Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) Chairman Ajay Seth has underscored the need to make health covers simpler, more transparent and easier for policyholders to understand and use.
Simplification of policy wording, strengthening underwriting at the point of sale to minimise claim issues arising from inadequate disclosures and facilitating hassle-free claim settlements were discussed by the Sub-Committee, of the Insurance Advisory Committee (IAC), at its meeting on August 28. The role of insurers, intermediaries, agents and TPAs in supporting policyholders at hospitals was also discussed, IRDAI said.
It also considered measures that will encourage insurers and hospitals to join the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX), including possible incentives linked to on-boarding, payments and faster settlement. Similarly, incentivising policyholders who undergo periodic health check-ups and adopt healthy practices was discussed while on the subject of preventive healthcare.
The meeting, third such of the sub-committee, emphasised the need for standardisation and enriching industry data to support evidence-based policy interventions. Noting assessment of claims and grievance outcomes should not focus solely on settlement ratios but also consider absolute values, it wanted insurers to consider publishing standard treatment guidelines (STGs) and treatment package rates towards facilitating more informed choices by policyholders. Among other things, the sub-committee comprising four-members and a few invitees from the insurance sector review of exclusions in favoured a further review of exclusions in the Customer Information Sheet to improve clarity and customer trust.
Setting the backdrop for the meeting was the report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare, headed by Rajya Sabha MP Ram Gopal Yadav, on ‘Affordability and accessibility of healthcare facilities in public and private sector’.
The Standing Committee, in the report presented earlier this month to the Parliament, noted the concerns around rising insurance premiums, exclusions and waiting periods, co-payments, claim rejections and the limited coverage of outpatient care, diagnostics and chronic disease management. An official note on the report said the Committee is concerned insurance claims charges very steeply for the same procedure between various hospitals. It strongly recommended for a transparent, well regulated health insurance sector where claim settlements date is integrated onto a common portal with open access as a measure to ensure transparency in the settlement of the claims.
It also recommended mandatory integration of all stakeholders-insurers, TPAs and healthcare providers into the NHCX to guarantee real-time, transparent claims processing even while calling for stringent regulatory penalties for arbitrary pricing and claim manipulation by insurers or empanelled hospitals, an official release on the report had said.

briefs.headline: Apparel exporters express concern over hike in cotton, yarn prices
briefs.bodyText:
Increase in cotton and yarn prices in the last six months is impacting the apparel value chain leading to even cancellation of garment export orders, claim apparel exporters.
Chairman of the Apparel Export Promotion Council (AEPC) A. Sakthivel said export of yarn and increase in cotton yarn prices is affecting the competitiveness of the apparel sector and hence, the Union government should regulate yarn exports.
Cotton yarn prices have increased by around 60 % since January. With increase in export of Indian cotton and cotton yarn to apparel-producing countries such as Bangladesh and Vietnam, Indian garment manufacturers are losing their competitiveness, he said.
R. Sakthivel, a garment exporter in Tiruppur, said cotton yarn prices increased by ₹7 a kg in March and in August by more than ₹17 a kg. In the last six months, the prices have gone up by ₹60 to ₹70 a kg. Garment exporters have entered into price contracts with the foreign buyers and cannot revise it now.
Due to recent supply and production issues in Bangladesh, some of the major international apparel importers began looking at India as an alternative sourcing destination. However, with continuous increase in yarn prices, price gap between India and Bangladesh widened and some of these orders were diverted to competing countries, he said.
Textile mills are revising yarn prices frequently and without prior notice and MSME units cannot buy yarn in bulk, say garment exporters.
Howevever, texile mills contend that hike in cotton prices is the reason for jump in yarn prices. Prices of the widely used Shankar 6 variety of cotton jumped 26 % in the last six months.

briefs.headline: HDFC Bank CEO Jagdishan to step down, decides not to seek reappointment
briefs.deck: The bank said it’s Board has decided to fast-track the process for selection and appointment of his successor well within time
briefs.bodyText:
HDFC Bank’s Sashidhar Jagdishan has conveyed his decision not to seek his re-appointment as the managing director & chief executive officer (MD&CEO) of the Bank, the largest private sector bank, said in an exchange filing.
“At its meeting held today, the Board of Directors took note of Mr. Sashidhar Jagdishan’s communication not to seek reappointment. Despite persuasion, Mr. Jagdishan reiterated his decision to not seek reappointment. Accordingly, he shall retire from the services of the Bank upon the close of business hours on October 26, 2026,” the bank said.
“The Board deeply appreciated his commitment, leadership, contribution to the growth and stability of the Bank and his role in the successful completion of one of the largest mergers in corporate India. The Board conveyed its best wishes to him in his future endeavors,” it added.
The bank said it’s Board has decided to fast-track the process for selection and appointment of his successor well within time.
Mr Jagdishan had taken over as the bank’s MD & CEO after the retirement of Aditya Puri.
Sashi, as he’s known to his friends and colleagues, joined HDFC Bank in 1996 and has played a critical role in its growth ever since.
Recently, he had come under criticism for the bank’s stock’s underperformance in the market and had faced allegations of violating corporate governance norms, which the bank had denied. In the last week, the stock had fallen to a multi-year low, according to brokers.
Earlier this year, the previous part-time chairman of the bank, Atanu Chakraborty, had resigned citing ethical grounds and following this Mr Sashidhar had come under the cloud.
Recently, he, the bank’s CFO and a top official were fined by the bank for “business overreach” after running an internal review into the bank’s deposit arrangements with Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) for garnering deposits in 2017 and 2021.
The Special Disciplinary Committee of Independent Directors had concluded that the conduct of the employees involved constituted business overreach rather than any mala fide action, personal enrichment, or improper motive.
The bank’s board had also communicated to the matter to Reserve Bank of India.
The RBI is also believed to have expressed discomfort with his continuation at the top post.
With only less than 2 months left for the completion of his tenure and no green signal coming from the board as well as the regulator, Mr. Jagdishan preferred to opt out, it is learnt.
Having started his tenure at the Bank as a manager in the Finance department, he became Business Head - Finance in 1999 and in 2008, the Chief Financial Officer of the Bank.
Prior to HDFC Bank, he worked with Deutsche Bank AG, Mumbai, for a period of three years.
It was during Mr. Jagdishan’s tenure that HDFC Ltd was merged with HDFC Bank in 2023, and the merger remained a drag on the bank’s performance due to high cost of funds raised by HDFC Ltd, the mortgage lender.
Earlier this week, a few U.S. law firms had initiated a class action suit relating to the MSRDC case.

briefs.headline: Zee’s Subhash Chandra accuses Mukesh Ambani of spreading misinformation, RIL denies allegations
briefs.deck: “His media company, TV18 Group, which includes CNBC, started this misinformation by broadcasting that NCLT has reduced Subhash Chandra’s ₹ 22,000 crore debt liability to only ₹6.5 crore,” says Subhash Chandra
briefs.bodyText:
Zee TV Group founder Subhash Chandra has accused Reliance Industries Ltd. (RIL) Chairman & Managing Director Mukesh Ambani and RIL owned media entities of orchestrating a misinformation campaign against him, causing disrepute.
Also Read: HDFC Bank plans to move NCLAT against NCLT order in Subhash Chandra case
In a video message aired on Zee News on Friday (August 28, 2026), Mr. Chandra, while naming Mr. Ambani, said, “His media company TV18 group, which includes CNBC, started this misinformation by broadcasting that NCLT has reduced Subhash Chandra’s ₹ 22,000 crore debt liability to only ₹6.5 crore.” RIL has denied the allegations.
In a statement, a company spokesperson said, “The Reliance Group has noted with dismay the baseless remarks by Essel Group [of which Zee is part] chairman Subhash Chandra. We strongly deny the allegations and insinuations against the media entities that are a part of the Reliance Group. Our media brands have never been used to attack anyone, nor will they ever be.” “We hold Subhash Chandra in high regard as a businessman and entrepreneur. We wish him well,” the spokesperson added.
In the video stating that he was putting the facts before the ‘people’s court’, Mr. Chandra said, “This is the same Mukesh Ambani whom I met to seek help when our issues [debt repayment obligation] started surfacing in January 2019. On the same day, his people brought down Zee’s share price [in the stock market] by 40%.”
“You cannot catch him because thousands of his web of benami companies are involved in stock operations,” he claimed.
Mr. Chandra alleged that Mr. Ambani wanted to acquire Zee TV in a wrong manner in connivance with Invesco, one of Zee’s investors.
He said he rejected an acquisition offer from Mr. Ambani as it was against the interests of minority shareholders. After that, Zee decided to merge with Sony because there was no other option left, he stated.
“As stated in a press release, our group companies and family members had a debt of ₹45,000 crore, out of which ₹43,000 crore has been repaid by selling our assets,” he said.

Emphasising that he was a proud corporate citizen of this country and had not run away despite financial stress, he said there was no other parallel of this size in repayment to creditors.
Again, turning his ire at Mr. Ambani, he said, “Mukesh Ji please stop the wrong propaganda against me and my group. I do not own anything now after implanting this NCLT order,” he said adding “I am left with nothing, and why are you harming me and trying to create issues. I have nothing to loose but you have a lot to loose.”
Stating that he can cause big harm to Mr. Ambani, he said he would defend if the witch hunt does not stop.
“You try to understand that you have large number of skeletons hidden in your cupboard. So please stop it and report anything which is right and do not do witch-hunt,” he warned.
He denied allegations that the government had accorded him any benefits in this case. “Despite all my trouble I had not asked any favour from the government,” he said.
Alleging that two Rajya Sabha MPs had been unleashed to question this NCLT ruling, he cautioned Mr. Ambani not to “play this game because it will come back to you one day.”

briefs.headline: From making iPhones to building the next Apple: Will India’s Rs 62,500 crore mobile phones bet pay off?
briefs.deck: With the launch of the Rs 62,500 crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS), India is eyeing its homegrown smartphone brands - with every aspect from design, R&D to components and manufacturing taking place in the country.
briefs.bodyText:
In 2020 when the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme was launched as a cornerstone of the ‘
Atmanirbhar Bharat
’ push, little did anyone know that smartphones would emerge as the poster boy of its success. Mobile phones assembly and manufacturing is arguably the biggest success story of the PLI scheme and now India is looking to take the next big leap in this space.
With the launch of the Rs 62,500 crore Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS), India is eyeing its homegrown smartphone brands - with every aspect from design, R&D to components and manufacturing taking place in the country. In fact, Electronics minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that by mid-2027, India expects its first strong indigenous mobile brand.
Bloomberg estimates from earlier this year suggest that Apple’s contract manufacturers now account for roughly three-fourths of India’s smartphone exports, playing a major role in the country’s emergence as one of the world’s fastest-growing hubs for handset exports.
Apple plans to ship most iPhones bound for the US from India by the end of the year, further strengthening India’s position as the leading source of smartphones sold in the US.
India's Rs 62,500 crore mobile phone push
For Prime Minister Narendra Modi, this shift represents a natural next stage for his government’s Make in India programme, and this is where the new scheme holds promise.
The focus is now moving beyond import substitution and domestic assembly towards a deeper integration with global supply chains, with the broader aim of positioning India as a manufacturing hub capable of competing with China.
Will the MPMS push India to build its own global smartphone brands like Apple, Samsung and others? We explore the potential of the new scheme:
What PLI scheme has achieved
Numbers have a telling story: Smartphones became India’s top exported individual commodity in FY 2025-26 overtaking even petroleum, gems and jewellery. They did not even feature in the top 100 exported commodities in 2014.
India is now the world's second-largest mobile phone manufacturer by volume, with 99.2% of phones used domestically made in India.
Experts see India’s PLI journey as transformational in establishing India as a global mobile phone manufacturing hub.
Prachir Singh, Senior Research Analyst, Counterpoint Research says that the PLI scheme has been instrumental in establishing India as a major global hub for mobile-phone manufacturing and assembly.
“While India was already adept at assembly before, the PLI scheme helped in increasing production, not just for the local market but for high-value exports,” he tells TOI.
Due to the PLI, India saw the rise of local players like Dixon, which was the top manufacturer in 2025 and was a recipient of the PLI benefits in the local manufacturers category.
What PLI scheme achieved for mobile phones manufacturing
On the other hand, it helped in significant export volume growth, at 27% CAGR between 2021-2025 driven by global giants Apple, Samsung and Motorola.
On the manufacturing end, it was led by beneficiaries of the PLI scheme which included Foxconn, TATA, Samsung and Dixon.
What PLI achieved was to accelerate large scale electronics manufacturing investments and exports, helping India emerge as the world’s second-largest mobile phone manufacturer by volume.
In 2014-15, only 26% of mobile phones sold in India were manufactured domestically; by December 2024, that figure had risen to 99.2%. The manufacturing ecosystem has also expanded from just 2 mobile phone manufacturing units in 2014 to more than 300 units today.
“The impact is particularly evident in the post-PLI period. Mobile phone production in India more than doubled from Rs 2.14 lakh crore in FY 2019-20 to Rs 5.5 lakh crore in FY 2024-25, reflecting the scale achieved through sustained investments and integration with global supply chains,” notes Saurabh Agarwal, Partner, EY India.
During the same period, India transitioned from primarily serving domestic demand to becoming a major export hub, with mobile phone exports increasing from Rs 1,566 crore in FY 2014-15 to Rs 1.2 lakh crore in FY 2023-24 and further to approximately Rs 2 lakh crore in FY 2024-25, making smartphones India's largest export product category.
What has been announced now
The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme is now the next step in India’s dream.
The Rs 62,500 crore outlay over a period of five years through FY 2030-31 aims to support the development of Indian-owned brands, domestic patents, product design and R&D.
The scheme promises support for scaling up of mobile phone production, with a particular focus on domestic value addition, further strengthening of supply chains, and ultimately improving India’s global competitiveness.
As part of the scheme, mobile phone manufacturers will get incentives ranging from 2.25% to 5% on eligible sales. There will be an additional incentive for sourcing components from domestic manufacturers. Yet another 3% incentive will be linked to product design and R&D.
The government has estimated that the scheme will help take the cumulative mobile phone production to around Rs 39 lakh crore during its five year tenure.
What is Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme?
Will this be the next transformative step?
Several things are coming together to aid the new dream, but execution will hold the key to the second phase of success.
MPMS comes at a time when investments under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) are beginning to materialise.
According to Saurabh Agarwal of EY India, many of the components and sub-assemblies covered under ECMS are also identified under MPMS for localisation-linked incentives.
This creates a powerful policy convergence: while ECMS is supporting the creation of domestic manufacturing capacity for components, MPMS is creating a large and predictable market for those products through localisation requirements and incentives.
“In that sense, MPMS is not merely a mobile phone manufacturing scheme; it is also a demand-generation mechanism that can accelerate the commercialisation of investments being made under ECMS,” he says.
Sohrab Bararia, Partner and Leader, Incentives Advisory, Grant Thornton Bharat cautions that execution of the new scheme is important to its success.
“The bigger challenge now is moving up the value chain and capturing a greater share of manufacturing, design, and technology development,” he tells TOI.
What makes MPMS different is its focus on domestic sourcing, in-house R&D, and capability building. India still relies on imports for several critical components, materials, and technologies, which limits value addition within the country.
“If the scheme succeeds in strengthening component manufacturing, encouraging innovation, and building local capabilities alongside assembly, it could help India evolve from an assembler of electronics to a true electronics powerhouse,” he says.
Prachir Singh of Counterpoint Research believes that moving from a manufacturing hub to a global electronics powerhouse will require a deeper transformation.
“India has made substantial progress in final assembly and exports, but needs to increase domestic value addition, localise components, develop semiconductor and component ecosystems, build stronger R&D and product-design capabilities,” he says.
The Rs 62,500 crore layout under the MPMS is likely to be a big enabler in this transformation, particularly as it links incentives to domestic sourcing of key components.
From Made in India to Made by India
Can India make its own Apple, Samsung?
So the big question is, will India be able to create its own world-class mobile phone brand like Apple, Samsung, or even Xiaomi?
The task is easier said than done, but scope remains, and it won’t happen overnight, feel experts.
Sohrab Bararia of Grant Thornton Bharat tells TOI, “Building a global brand is about much more than incentives. It takes years of innovation, product development, customer trust, marketing, and a strong ecosystem around the brand.”
What MPMS does is create some of the building blocks needed for that journey. Its focus on domestic sourcing, in-house R&D, and capability building is a step in the right direction. Over time, this can help Indian companies develop their own products, technologies, and intellectual property rather than just assemble devices.
“Ultimately, success will depend on how the market responds. Consumers buy brands like Apple and Samsung not just because of where they are manufactured, but because of the innovation, quality, and customer experience they offer,” he says.
“If Indian brands can deliver on those aspects while leveraging the support provided under MPMS, the scheme could well be the first step towards creating globally recognised Indian electronics champions,” he adds.
Prachir Singh also thinks that creating an Indian Xiaomi, Samsung or Apple will be challenging. MPMS will support the manufacturing ecosystem, but building globally competitive Indian brands will ultimately depend on private-sector execution, he says.
Saurabh Agarwal of India is more confident that the new scheme significantly improves India’s chances of creating globally competitive mobile phone brands, although it should be viewed as a long-term opportunity rather than an immediate outcome.
“The biggest limitation of previous incentive programmes was that they were primarily focused on scaling manufacturing. MPMS is different because it explicitly supports Indian brands, design, R&D and intellectual property creation,” he tells TOI.
This is important because global leaders such as Apple, Samsung and Xiaomi were built not only through manufacturing scale, but through sustained investment in technology, product development, brand-building and ownership of IP.
“MPMS is the first policy framework that directly targets these value drivers. India also enters this phase from a position of considerable strength. The country has already built a world-class manufacturing ecosystem. A large domestic market, deep engineering talent, a mature digital ecosystem and a growing electronics supply chain provide many of the building blocks that successful global technology brands require,” he adds.
What makes the opportunity particularly compelling is that India is no longer trying to create domestic brands in the absence of a manufacturing ecosystem. Unlike a decade ago, Indian companies can now leverage an established supplier base, large-scale production capabilities and access to global markets. MPMS seeks to build on this foundation by encouraging Indian firms to move beyond assembly and invest in product ownership, technology and innovation.
So, will the scheme create the next Apple or Samsung overnight? Probably not. But it can create the conditions for the emergence of globally recognised Indian brands over the next decade, experts say.

stories.headline: ‘He does not depend on the pitch’: Rahane explains why Suthar can thrive anywhere
stories.deck: Manav Suthar has impressed in his first three Test matches, taking 23 wickets. His ability to generate drift and deceive batters is a significant strength. Ajinkya Rahane noted Suthar's effectiveness regardless of pitch conditions and his quick learning. Suthar's adaptability strengthens his prospects for a larger role in India's spin attack. The team faces a challenging series in New Zealand…
stories.bodyText:
Manav Suthar has wasted little time making an impression in Test cricket, with the left-arm spinner already putting himself in the conversation for a bigger role in India’s red-ball plans.
Suthar has claimed 23 wickets from his first three Tests, but his impact has gone beyond the numbers. His ability to generate drift, combine it with a deceptive release and consistently hit the right areas has made him an awkward proposition for batters.
Ajinkya Rahane
 has been particularly impressed by the early signs from the youngster. The former India captain believes Suthar’s biggest strength could be his ability to remain effective without relying heavily on assistance from the pitch.
"I have noticed two things about Manav. The first thing is that for him, the pitch does not matter, whether it turns or not. His speed through the air helps him deceive the batters. It is important and good that you do not depend on the wicket as a spinner. Then you can do well in any condition. The other thing was the way he altered the speed. He has been a quick learner in just three games. He bowled differently to each batter and used the angles well.
 Yes, it is early, but he has done well," he said in a video on his Hindi YouTube Channel.
Suthar making a case for bigger role
The 23 wickets in three matches have given Suthar an impressive beginning to his international career, while his adaptability has added another dimension to his prospects.
Suthar’s early performances have already established him as India’s lead spinner. Even during the Sri Lanka tour, he was captain Shubman Gill’s first choice whenever the team needed wickets. Since 
Ravindra Jadeja
 is gradually becoming more of a batting all-rounder—especially in overseas conditions, Suthar is expected to be India's leading spinner for the near future.
His ability to adjust his pace, angles and approach according to the batter has particularly stood out, strengthening the argument that he can be effective across different conditions.
Rahane warns India of New Zealand challenge
Rahane also turned his attention to India’s next Test assignment in New Zealand, where the conditions are expected to be considerably different from those the team experienced in Sri Lanka.
The former India batter believes adapting quickly to the conditions will be central to India’s preparations. He also highlighted the value of match practice ahead of a challenging series.
"The conditions will be totally different in New Zealand. You need to read the wicket and adapt that way. In the last five to six years, we have seen that the team adapts well. I expect them to prepare well. The good thing was that they played a practice match in Sri Lanka. If they get the time for that in New Zealand too, it will be very crucial for mental and physical preparation, even skill-wise," he expressed.
For Suthar, however, the immediate task is to build on an encouraging start. Three Tests and 23 wickets have already given him a platform, while his ability to produce results without depending solely on turning pitches could prove valuable as India look to strengthen their spin options for the future.

stories.headline: 2026 Ballon D'Or Race: Mourinho backs Mbappé over UCL and World Cup winners
stories.deck: José Mourinho has backed Kylian Mbappé for the 2026 Ballon d’Or, arguing that individual brilliance should outweigh team trophies. Mbappé’s record-breaking World Cup, plus his prolific La Liga and Champions League campaigns, strengthens his case. Mourinho insists the award should recognise the world’s best player rather than automatically rewarding those who win the Champions League or World Cup.
stories.bodyText:
José Mourinho has thrown his support behind Kylian Mbappé to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or, with the Real Madrid manager arguing that the award should recognise the best individual player in the world rather than simply going to someone who lifted the 
Champions League
 or World Cup.
Mourinho made the case for his own striker ahead of Real Madrid’s La Liga meeting with Málaga on Sunday, pointing to Mbappé’s remarkable individual year and, in particular, the history he made with France at the World Cup. The comments also put Mbappé ahead of several leading contenders from Paris Saint-Germain and Spain in Mourinho’s assessment of who truly deserves the prize.
The Ballon d’Or is generally judged on three broad criteria: individual performance, team achievements, and class and fair play. Individual performance covers a player’s goals, assists, influence and consistency; team achievements consider major club and international trophies, as well as the player’s contribution to them; and class and fair play include sportsmanship, conduct and public image.
Mourinho: Mbappé has already made history
Mourinho believes Mbappé has a particularly strong claim because of what he achieved individually this summer, even though France did not win the World Cup.
“For me, there is one who, individually, made history this summer,” Mourinho said, referring to Mbappé becoming the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history.
The France captain finished last season as the top scorer in both La Liga and the Champions League before taking that scoring form onto the international stage. He also scored a hat-trick in Real Madrid's 4-1 victory over Real Sociedad on Wednesday, giving him an immediate boost as the new campaign gets underway.
Mbappé's 2025-26 season was already extraordinary before the World Cup. He scored 43 goals in 47 appearances for Real Madrid across all competitions and finished as the leading scorer in both La Liga and the Champions League.
His World Cup campaign strengthened his case further, with 10 goals in eight appearances making him the tournament's leading scorer and taking him to the top of the World Cup's all-time scoring charts.
Those numbers place Mbappé strongly under the individual-performance criterion, which rewards sustained excellence, attacking output and a player's overall influence throughout the season.
Real Madrid's Bernardo Silva, left, and Kylian Mbappe celebrate after scoring during the La Liga soccer match between Real Madrid and Real Sociedad in Madrid, Spain, Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez)
Mourinho's argument: the Ballon d'Or should not simply follow trophies
Mbappé's biggest problem in the Ballon d'Or race is that, despite his individual numbers, he did not win a major trophy last season, while some of his rivals played starring roles in teams that lifted the biggest prizes.
Paris Saint-Germain won the Champions League, while Spain won the World Cup, putting players such as PSG's Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, along with Spain midfielder Rodri, firmly into the conversation.
Mourinho, however, does not believe winning those competitions should automatically decide the award.
“The best players in the world, there are two, three or four of them, and we know who they are: they’re here,” the Real Madrid manager said, indicating that several of the leading candidates are part of his squad.
“You cannot give the Ballon d’Or to a player simply because he won the Champions League or the World Cup,” he added.
Mourinho framed the award as something that should recognise players whose individual greatness lasts well beyond the trophies they collect during their careers.
“The Ballon d'Or should go to one of those players who, when they retire, we miss them for eternity. Maradona, Cristiano, Messi, R9, Zidane... You can't give the Ballon d'Or to a guy just for winning the UCL or the World Cup.”
The Real Madrid manager then took the argument a step further, suggesting that if the award were simply about rewarding the winners of those competitions, then the coaches responsible for those victories would deserve recognition instead.
“If we want to reward the Champions League, then give it to Luis Enrique. For the Spanish national team, give it to [Luis] De la Fuente. The best player in the world is something else and he is neither at PSG nor in the Spain team.”
Team achievements remain an important part of the award's criteria, but Mourinho's position is that collective success should be weighed alongside a player's personal contribution rather than used as an automatic shortcut to victory.
Mbappé faces a strong field
Mbappé is expected to be among the leading names when the 30-player Ballon d'Or shortlist is announced, although he faces competition from several stars who can point to major trophies as part of their cases.
Dembélé and Kvaratskhelia have the Champions League title with PSG behind them, while Rodri was part of Spain's World Cup-winning side. England striker Harry Kane is another major contender after his prolific campaign.
Mourinho's own squad also gives him several players who could feature prominently in the voting. Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham are both expected to be in contention alongside Mbappé, meaning Real Madrid could have multiple representatives near the top of the rankings.
The third criterion, class and fair play, can also influence how a candidate is viewed. It includes a player's behaviour on the pitch, relationship with opponents and officials, conduct away from football and wider public image. Mbappé's leadership as France captain and his standing as one of the sport's most prominent figures will form part of the broader discussion around his candidacy.
Mbappé has never won the Ballon d'Or
A victory would also give Mbappé the individual honour that has so far eluded him despite spending years among the world's elite.
The Frenchman has consistently featured in Ballon d'Or discussions but has never claimed the prize, and his 2025-26 campaign gave him perhaps his strongest case yet.
Now, after finishing as the leading scorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup and becoming the tournament's all-time leading scorer, he enters this year's race with Mourinho publicly arguing that those individual achievements should outweigh the trophies won by his rivals.
Real Madrid host Málaga on Sunday as Mourinho's side look for a third consecutive victory to begin their La Liga campaign, with Mbappé arriving into the match fresh from his hat-trick against Real Sociedad and firmly at the centre of the Ballon d'Or conversation.

stories.headline: Dortmund cruise to win as Elversberg claim historic victory in Bundesliga
stories.deck: Guirassy provided ⁠a clinical finish inside the opening nine minutes to settle Dortmund, before new signing Konstantelias fired in ‌a shot that took a deflection off a defender and into the net
stories.bodyText:
Goals from Serhou Guirassy and Giannis Konstantelias steered Borussia Dortmund to a 2-0 victory over Hamburg in their Bundesliga season-opener on Saturday (August 29, 2026), while there were also wins for RB Leipzig and promoted Elversberg.
Guirassy provided a clinical finish inside the opening nine minutes to settle Dortmund, before new signing Konstantelias fired in a shot that took a deflection off a defender and into the net.
Dortmund finished the game with 10 men when Samuele Inacio received a straight red card three minutes after coming off the bench for a dangerous tackle, but were able to complete the win.
Elversberg, from a town of just 13,000 people, made a dream Bundesliga debut with a 3-2 victory over Bayer Leverkusen.
They raced into an early 2-0 lead after goals from Lukas Petkov and Cole Campbell, and then added a third in the 46th minute through David Mokwa.
Leverkusen pulled a goal back 13 minutes from the end through Patrik Schick and Christian Kofane netted a second in added time.
Leipzig defeated Borussia Moenchengladbach 3-0 with Ridle Baku, Antonio Nusa and Rocco Reitz all on target, the latter against his former side.
Mainz and Paderborn played to a 0-0 draw, while Tim Skarke scored a 92nd equaliser for Union Berlin in their 3-3 draw with Eintracht Frankfurt.
The latter led 3-1 in the 67th minute thanks to Younes Ebnoutalib’s hat-trick, but could not hold on for the away win.
Thijs Dallinga scored twice in the final 18 minutes to secure a 3-2 win for Cologne over Hoffenheim.
Bayern Munich started their league season on Friday with a thumping 5-1 win over Stuttgart.

stories.headline: Women’s Hockey World Cup | Argentina breaks Dutch hearts in a shootout
stories.bodyText:
On a chilly summer evening at the Wagener Stadion, Argentina’s women had their own Maracanazo moment. Netherlands does not lose often. In the last 13 years, it has lost just one game a year while lifting three successive World Cups.
On Saturday, too, Netherlands was on the verge of winning before Argentina struck late to hold it to a 1-1 draw. The Argentines went on to dethrone the Dutch in a penalty shootout.
After Cristina Cosentino saved two Netherlands penalties, Sofia Cairo made it 3-1 when she put the ball in the net and sparked celebrations in the Argentina camp.
It was doubly sweet for the South American nation as it avenged its 2022 final loss while also silencing a partisan home crowd at one of the cathedrals of the sport.
In a highly anticipated rematch, both teams struggled to impose themselves in open play as they looked overawed by the occasion. It was left to the talismanic dragflickers to have their say in penalty corners.
It needed 30 minutes for the first one to arrive. Yibbi Jansen didn’t even need a sighter and the tournament’s top-scorer sounded the boards to hoist the lead for the host.
In response, Argentina’s penalty corner set-up squandered four chances in the third quarter.
But, the South Americans continued to push on through Cairo, whose snaking runs into the circle troubled the home side’s defence and earned many penalty corners.
With seven minutes to go, Argentina opted for a variation. Agustina Gorzelany fired her dragpush into the path of a teammate, who deflected the ball to an unmarked Maria Granatto for the equaliser.
In the third-place play-off, co-host Belgium beat Australia 1-0 through a goal from Charlotte Engelbert.
The result (final): Netherlands 1 (Yibbi Jansen 30-pc) drew with Argentina 1 (Maria Granatto 53-pc). Argentina won 3-1 on penalties.

briefs.headline: José Mourinho says Ballon d’Or shouldn’t go to player just for winning UCL or WC
briefs.deck: Jose Mourinho has challenged the traditional Ballon d’Or criteria, arguing that the award should recognise individual greatness rather than simply major trophies. The Real Madrid manager believes several of his players belong among the world’s elite, with Kylian Mbappé emerging as a leading contender after a remarkable 2025-26 season and outstanding World Cup performance.
briefs.bodyText:
With the 2026 Ballon d’Or drawing closer, Jose Mourinho has offered a rather different way of looking at football’s biggest individual prize, arguing that winning the Champions League or World Cup should not automatically put a player at the front of the queue. The Real Madrid manager believes the award should recognise the players who stand out at the very highest level and leave a lasting mark on the sport, rather than simply rewarding whoever happened to collect the biggest trophies.
Mourinho made the comments during his press conference ahead of Real Madrid’s LaLiga meeting with newly promoted Malaga, where he also suggested that some of the strongest Ballon d’Or candidates are already playing under him at the Santiago Bernabéu.
Mourinho wants the award to recognise greatness, not just trophies
Mourinho's argument is rooted in the idea that the Ballon d’Or should belong to players whose careers and performances make them impossible to forget, rather than someone whose main case rests on winning a major competition.
"The Ballon d'Or should go to one of those players who, when they retire, we miss them for eternity. Maradona, Cristiano, Messi, R9, Zidane... You can't give the Ballon d'Or to a guy just for winning the UCL or the World Cup. 
If you should give it to someone just for winning the UCL, then give it to Luis Enrique."
He then made it clear that, in his view, the award should not become a contest based on nationality, club or the biggest trophy won during the season.
"No, it needs to go to the best player in the world, not necessarily a Spanish guy, or a PSG player. It needs to go to one of the 3-4 best players in the world, and those guys are here. But politics come into the Ballon d'Or, so I don't like getting into politics."
Mourinho's comments touch on a long-running debate surrounding the award, where players whose teams win the Champions League, World Cup or other major honours can often gain a significant advantage in the voting, even when another player may have produced a stronger individual season.
Who does Mourinho believe can win it?
Although Mourinho did not name a single player as the only deserving candidate in his broader comments, his reference to the "3-4 best players in the world" being at Real Madrid points towards a number of his own stars, including Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham.
Mbappé, in particular, has a compelling case after a remarkable 2025-26 campaign. The French forward scored 43 goals in 47 appearances for Real Madrid across all competitions, while also winning both the LaLiga Golden Boot and the Champions League Golden Boot.
His year became even more extraordinary at international level during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mbappé scored 10 goals in eight appearances, becoming the first player to reach double figures at a World Cup tournament in the 21st century and moving to the top of the competition's all-time scoring charts.
That form has continued into the new campaign, with Mbappé recently scoring a hat-trick against Real Sociedad.
For a player who has spent much of the past decade being discussed among the world's elite but has never won the Ballon d’Or, the timing could hardly be more interesting.
Real Madrid will return to LaLiga action on Sunday, August 30, when they host Málaga CF at the Santiago Bernabéu. Kick-off is scheduled for 8:30 PM IST (5:00 PM local time), with Mourinho and his squad looking to continue their campaign in Spain’s top flight.

briefs.headline: Women’s Hockey WC: Argentina stun Netherlands in shootout to win third title
briefs.deck: Argentina's women's hockey team secured a remarkable World Cup victory on Saturday. They defeated the top-ranked Netherlands team in a thrilling final match. Goalkeeper Cristina Cosentino was instrumental in the team's stunning upset win. Argentina clinched their third World Cup title after a tense shoot-out. Belgium secured third place by beating Australia in their match.
briefs.bodyText:
Argentina women’s hockey team achieved a miracle on Saturday as they beat world No. 1 and three-time defending champions Netherlands in the World Cup final at Wagener Stadium in Amstelveen to lift the title for the third time.
Playing in front of a raucous crowd, the South Americans were crowned world champions after winning 3-1 in a shoot-out, following a 1-1 draw at the end of 60 minutes. Goalkeeper Cristina Cosentino was the star, producing a string of superb saves — during the shoot-out as well as in regulation time — to help Argentina pull off the upset.
Cosentino was duly named Player of the Match and, speaking after the game, could not have been prouder of her teammates and what they had achieved.
After all, this was the first time since 2010 that the Dutch women lost a World Cup final. And 16 years ago, it was Argentina who had beaten them to claim the title for the second time — their first coming in 2002, also by defeating Netherlands.
On Saturday, however, it seemed for a long time that Argentina would not be able to repeat that feat. They had lost the 2022 final too, and it looked like history was going to repeat itself as Netherlands took the lead in the 30th minute through Yibbi Jansen from a penalty corner and continued to hold on to their advantage well into the final quarter.
But Argentina simply refused to give up.
They kept pushing the Dutch back and won numerous PCs. The Dutch defence held firm for much of the contest, but eventually Argentina found a way through in the 54th minute.
Following their seventh penalty corner, a mistrap saw Agustina Gorzelany fire the ball towards goal. A Dutch defender managed to get a stick to it, but the ball fell to Maria Granatto, who made no mistake from the left of the D, finding the back of the net to bring Argentina level with six minutes remaining.
The equaliser appeared to shake the Dutch, who completely lost their composure in the shoot-out.
Pien Sanders, Felice Albers and Freeke Moes all failed to convert their attempts as Cosentino produced a sensational performance in goal. For Argentina, Zoe Diaz’s effort was ruled out for backstick, but Victoria Granatto, Brisa Bruggesser and Sofia Cairo all found the net to seal a 3-1 victory.
Earlier, the final was a cagey affair, with neither side creating too many clear-cut opportunities. Late in the first quarter, Pien Dicke had a couple of chances, but Cosentino stood firm to keep the Dutch at bay.
Jansen eventually gave the Dutch the lead late in the second quarter, but they were unable to impose the kind of control they are renowned for.
Argentina, meanwhile, kept believing and pushing until they finally found a way back into the contest. And when the shoot-out arrived, Cosentino produced the defining moments to help Argentina complete a stunning victory and lift their third World Cup title.
Meanwhile, in the other match of the day, Belgium beat Australia 1-0 to finish in third place.

briefs.headline: Squash | This is the best I have played in terms of quality and consistency: Velavan Senthilkumar
briefs.bodyText:
Sparring with World No. 15 Mohamed ElShorbagy and World No. 22 Baptiste Masotti under the watchful eyes of French coach Gregory Gaultier in Prague over the last few weeks has made India’s Velavan Senthilkumar a more solid and consistent player.
The 28-year-old’s preparation ahead of the new season paid handsome dividends as he clinched his maiden PSA World Tour title at the Budapest Open on Friday. In the Copper event, the World No. 54 defeated Hungary’s Balazs Farkas 11-4, 11-2, 11-3 in the final to bag his 11th PSA crown.
On winning the biggest trophy of his career yet, Velavan said: “This is the best I’ve played in terms of the quality of squash and the consistency I displayed.”
Working with Gaultier, a former World No. 1, and Saurav Ghosal helped him immensely. “With Gaultier, I am putting in the hard yards and with Saurav, I am working on a few technical aspects,” he said.
Beating top seed Eain Yow Ng of Malaysia for the first time — in the last-eight stage — was a huge confidence booster for the Indian. “I have grown up with him playing the Asian juniors. This was my first win against him,” he added.
Velavan proved that the victory over the Malaysian was no flash in the pan as he defeated his compatriot and third seed Veer Chotrani in the semifinals. “That was another amazing match. I was down 8-10 in the fifth game. Eventually winning it 12-10 was a really good indicator [of how I played],” he said.
His ultimate goal is to break into the world’s top 20 by the end of the season.
Excited
The southpaw is excited to play with Joshna Chinappa in mixed doubles at the Asian Games. “She is the most experienced player in the Indian team. She knows all the subtleties of doubles. I am trying to learn all of that from her,” said Velavan, who had won bronze with Joshna at the Asian Doubles Championships in June.

briefs.headline: John Cena reveals he and The Rock ‘hated each other’ before WrestleMania showdown
briefs.deck: John Cena openly acknowledged the animosity that brewed before his WrestleMania 28 clash with The Rock. Their competitive rivalry escalated beyond the ring, leading to personal jabs and near confrontations backstage during heated promo exchanges. Although Cena publicly insisted he would prevail, he privately recognized The Rock's impending victory. After the match, heartfelt apologies paved the…
briefs.bodyText:
John Cena
 and 
The Rock
 are now viewed as WWE legends who share plenty of mutual respect. But before that relationship developed, the road to their WrestleMania 28 showdown was filled with genuine tension, with Cena admitting that the hostility between them was not entirely part of the script.
For more than a year, the two traded personal shots before finally meeting in the main event in Miami. Fans understood they were watching a manufactured rivalry play out. Cena later revealed the bad blood underneath it was real enough to worry him.
Cena admits the hatred was real
Cena has explained that the promos sometimes tipped over from sports entertainment into something more personal.
"During a lot of moments leading up to that fight, we crossed the line of sports entertainment, and people could tell that we really hated each other," Cena said.
The two men, by his own account, held genuinely different opinions of one another at the time. "Even though he had always been cordial to me, I did something foolish and started drumming up rumours about things I had no idea about," Cena added.
None of this was standard promotional trash talk. Cena had publicly questioned The Rock's commitment to 
WWE
 after the former champion left to build a career in Hollywood.
Why Cena had a problem with The Rock
The Rock had walked away from the ring and become one of the biggest names in film. 
Cena, meanwhile, had settled into the role of WWE's leading full-time babyface, the guy who never left.
He was particularly critical of The Rock pursuing acting while still talking up his love for wrestling. In 2010, Cena said: "He's genuinely nice guy. I've met him, and he's a fantastic human being."
Then came the sting. He questioned why The Rock couldn't return for major occasions: "Just, don't f*** me around and tell me that you love [wrestling] when you're just doing it to do something else." Those comments became the fuel for everything that followed.
Nearly coming to blows
When The Rock came back in 2011, it was first as host of WrestleMania 27. That involvement quickly hardened into a rivalry with Cena, setting up their meeting a year later.
Things escalated through their promo battles on Raw. At one point Cena mocked The Rock for apparently using notes on his arm to remember lines, a jab that visibly angered him, and the confrontation reportedly turned heated backstage.
Both men have since admitted how close it came to boiling over. "We might fail miserably at it," The Rock said of the risky approach they took to the rivalry. "But in this case it worked out very well and through all that edge and attitude and bite that we had and nearly coming to blows backstage and one night in the ring." He remembers the face-off getting genuinely intense: "Literally, we were nose-to-nose, it was any second."
Cena knew The Rock would win
For a year, Cena publicly insisted there was no way The Rock would beat him. Privately, he'd known the outcome almost from the start.
"For a year straight I kept telling people that there is no way he was going to beat me, but I knew that he was going to win the moment the feud started," Cena said.
However, reports at the time suggested WWE had initially considered having Cena win at WrestleMania 28 before changing course around the event. The final decision saw The Rock emerge victorious in his home state of Florida. Former referee Mike Chioda later recalled some backstage tension around the decision, with Cena having carried WWE as its full-time star for years before being asked to lose to a returning Rock.
Cena apologised after losing
Once The Rock had pinned him, Cena did something that reshaped their relationship going forward. "The first thing I did after he beat me was apologise to his mother," he revealed. Then he walked straight into The Rock's locker room. "Then I went right into Dwayne's locker room and apologised to him."
It didn't end the feud outright. The Rock beat CM Punk for the title at the following year's Royal Rumble, setting up a rematch at WrestleMania 29. This time Cena won.
From genuine enemies to friends
The rematch closed the book on the rivalry. Somewhere in the years after, genuine respect crept in, and eventually something like friendship, an odd outcome given how personal things had briefly become.
There's an irony worth sitting with too. Cena spent years criticising The Rock for chasing Hollywood over wrestling. He later walked almost the same path himself, building a film career while trimming back his WWE schedule.
None of this made Cena versus Rock memorable purely because of the size of the matches. It was that, for a stretch, nobody quite knew where the storyline ended and the real animosity began.

briefs.headline: ‘A little jealous’: Sunil Chhetri on India’s chance to play Brazil, Uruguay
briefs.deck: Sunil Chhetri, the revered former captain, expresses a nuanced envy as he observes the current Indian football team gearing up for matches against legendary opponents like Brazil and Uruguay. He emphasises the importance of these unique encounters and encourages young players to make the most of this chance. Chhetri has confidence in the coach's choices and urges a united front for a brighter…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Former India captain 
Sunil Chhetri
 has admitted he feels “a little jealous” watching the current generation get an opportunity to face footballing giants Brazil and Uruguay, revealing that he never got such a chance during his long international career.
India are scheduled to host five-time world champions Brazil on October 3 and Uruguay three days later at Kolkata’s Salt Lake Stadium. The high-profile fixtures will give a young Indian side a rare opportunity to test itself against two of South America's biggest footballing nations.
“I feel a little jealous as a spectator. In my 24-26 years as a professional and nearly 20 years with the national team, I never got an opportunity like this,” Chhetri told the All India Football Federation (AIFF).
The former striker, who retired from international football last year, urged the current players to stay fit, compete with determination and make the most of the opportunity. Despite being away from the national-team setup, Chhetri said he remained confident in the squad's young talent.
“This is their time. There are so many talented youngsters in the team. Everyone gets their opportunity; just like I got mine 20 years ago,” he said.
Chhetri backs coach, rules out comeback
Chhetri also refused to second-guess the coaching staff when asked about selection decisions and the omission of certain players, insisting that the coach was best placed to assess the team's requirements.
“The coach has to answer that. I'm just a fan now, watching like everyone else,” he said.
The 42-year-old, who recently returned to training, also dismissed any immediate prospect of making a comeback with a touch of humour.
“I just trained for 20 minutes. I'm around 42 now, I can barely run properly and I'm struggling,” he joked.
The Brazil and Uruguay fixtures come at a difficult time for Indian football, with the side currently ranked 138th in the FIFA rankings and uncertainty surrounding the domestic calendar. Chhetri, however, called for optimism and collective responsibility rather than a blame game.
“The Indian football graph, for as many years as I’ve played, has always been like this. We’re probably in a phase where things are not going very well, because of what we’ve done with the national team, what we’ve done in the league, etcetera. But we all have to be hopeful,” he said on the sidelines of the Football Players' Association of India's Indian Football Awards 2026.
“At the end of the day, it’s going to be fine. It takes time. Looking at all your faces, we all want things to be fine as soon as possible. It will be. I’m always hopeful. Things might be a little bit 'kharab' (bad), but things are going to be fine.”
Chhetri also accepted that players must take responsibility for the team's struggles.
“I was also a part of the national team. And why has the ranking gone down? It’s because of the way we have played, the games that we should have won but lost. That is the reason why we are where we are. As players, we take responsibility. I took it when I was there,” he said.

briefs.headline: DULEEP TROPHY | Semifinals promise much as Central battles East and South spars with North
briefs.bodyText:
:
The cream of Indian cricket’s second rung will be in action as the 2026-27 Duleep Trophy semifinal fixtures get underway at the BCCI Centre of Excellence from Sunday.
Defending champion Central Zone will take on East while last season’s finalist South Zone will spar with North.
East and North notched up contrasting victories in the quarterfinals. Where East, marshalled by Ishan Kishan, recorded a thumping innings and 210-run win over North East, Kanhaiya Wadhawan’s North conjured a dramatic 52-run success despite West Zone coasting at 195 for three while chasing 287.
Teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi could only score eight runs for East but picked up two wickets with his left-arm spin in the second essay. The last-four clash will offer him another opportunity at bettering his middling First Class numbers (215 runs from 13 innings at average of 16.53).
Keeping him silent will be high on Central skipper Rajat Patidar’s priorities, and it remains to be seen if off-spinner Saransh Jain can aid him in this. Saransh is part of the roster but made his India debut in the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo, which kept him on the field until Thursday.
But fellow India international Gurnoor Brar — who didn’t play either Test in Sri Lanka — has been added to the North Zone squad and participated in Saturday morning’s practise. His entry further bolsters North’s pace attack, for it already has Anshul Kamboj and Arshdeep Singh.
Jammu & Kashmir left-arm spinner Abid Mushtaq starred in the win over West with a match-haul of nine for 99. Whether he gets the same purchase at CoE Ground 2 as he did on the red-soil wicket at Ground 1 will be intriguing to watch.
South has a solid batting line-up, led by skipper Tilak Varma, R. Smaran — 2025-26 Ranji Trophy’s leading scorer with 950 runs — and Karun Nair. There is also Shaik Rasheed, the highly rated 21-year-old, who made 627 runs in Andhra’s dash to the Ranji quarterfinals last season.

briefs.headline: ‘He could be in the realms of Lara and Tendulkar’: Boycott’s big Brook warning
briefs.deck: Sir Geoffrey Boycott has high praise for Harry Brook's exceptional batting skills but expresses concern that Brook isn't fully harnessing his potential in Test cricket. He believes Brook's style is too reminiscent of white-ball play, suggesting it could hinder his development. Boycott sees similarities between Brook and legendary players like Lara and Tendulkar but laments that his advice went…
briefs.bodyText:
England legend Sir Geoffrey Boycott believes 
Harry Brook
 possesses the rare batting ability to reach the heights of 
Sachin Tendulkar
 and 
Brian Lara
, but fears the current world No. 1 Test batter is not making the most of his extraordinary talent.
Boycott, who played 108 Tests and 36 ODIs for England, has been particularly critical of Brook's approach in Test cricket. While acknowledging his exceptional timing, range of shots and reach, the former England captain believes Brook's decision-making and tendency to approach Test deliveries like a white-ball batter are preventing him from fulfilling his enormous potential.
“I've said before and I'll say again, I've seen a lot of players. I haven't seen anybody with the talent he's got for a long time. Enormous talent. The timing, the shot playing, he's tall, big reach, but his thinking is just unbelievable,” Boycott said in the ‘Geoffrey Boycott: An Extraordinary Innings’ podcast.
‘He could be in the realms of Lara and Tendulkar’
Brook remains ranked the world's No. 1 Test batter, but his recent run has not matched the remarkable standards he has set in the format. He has gone more than a year without a Test century. 
In the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley, Brook scored 91, before making 15 in the ongoing Test at Lord’s.
For Boycott, the issue is not a lack of ability but how Brook chooses to use it. The former opener believes the England batter has the talent to join a very exclusive group of all-time greats if he can improve his thinking and become more selective in Test cricket.
“If he wants to carry on playing that way, he'll have a decent career, but he has the ability, if he could think better, to be in the realms of Lara and Tendulkar. And, whoa, that's a bit special. To be up in that stratosphere is huge,” Boycott said.
“There ain't many above them, except Bradman, and that's special. But he plays one-day cricket to every ball. He doesn't have a look at the ball, he has to bash the first ball. He'll just keep getting caught at mid-off and mid-on and daft places,” he added.
Boycott's criticism centres on what he sees as Brook's inability to make the necessary adjustment between white-ball and Test cricket. Brook is also England's white-ball captain, and Boycott believes the aggressive instincts that have served him in limited-overs cricket can become a liability in the longer format.
Boycott offered to help — but heard nothing
Boycott also revealed that he had previously been offered an opportunity to speak to Brook about his Test batting, but the conversation never materialised.
According to Boycott, Brook's uncle approached him last year and asked whether he would speak to the England batter. Boycott said he was happy to help if Brook wanted his advice, but he did not want to impose himself.
“His uncle came to me last year and he said, 'Would you have a word with him?' Well, he asked me what I thought of him. I told him exactly this. He said, 'Really?' I said, 'Yeah.' I said that much ability is rare, special.
“He said, 'Would you have a word with him?' I said, 'It's not for me to go to him. He might tell me to, you know, off,' I said. But if he asked me, of course I'd help. Why would I not? I gave him my number and never heard a word,” Boycott said.

briefs.headline: TNPL | Kovai Kings bowl rivals over in victorious campaign
briefs.bodyText:
Batters win you games, but bowlers win you tournaments. In TNPL-10, Vida Kovai Kings proved it right as its potent bowling attack secured its third title in five years, beating Madurai Panthers by 82 runs in the final here on Friday.
The title decider began with a glitzy closing ceremony, and in the end, it was M. Shahrukh Khan’s men who shone brightly under lights.
Since 2022, Shahrukh has led the franchise to the summit clash on four occasions, underscoring its consistency. Despite a mega auction in between, the team managed to retain its core group of players while also adding some exciting talents.
Apart from the skipper, top-order batter B. Sachin and spinners M. Siddharth and Jhathavedh Subramanyan were part of the set-up which last won in 2023, and their experience proved handy in the end.
Sachin shouldered the batting load in the first part of the season, and once the others started to chip in, Kovai Kings’ bowling attack could bundle out opponents easily.
As far as the tournament as a whole is concerned, one criticism it faced in recent years was that the pitches were not conducive for high-scoring games, which in turn affected the batters’ development in the shortest format.
Although the competition was played at only two venues this year, the surfaces were batting-friendly and saw the most runs scored in a single edition.
Amongst youngsters, the biggest positive was the emergence of pacer D. Deepesh, who clocked speeds in excess of 140 kph. The 18-year-old’s rise should excite TN ahead of the domestic season.
Since its third SMAT title in 2021, TN’s fortunes in T20 cricket have dipped drastically, and it has failed to qualify for the knockouts ever since. As the State team looks to regain its footing at the National level, it remains to be seen if some of the performers in the league can deliver at a bigger stage.
Awards: Highest wicket-taker: Deeban Lingesh (Kovai Kings); Highest run-scorer: B. Sachin (Kovai Kings); Most dependable player: Deeban Lingesh (Kovai Kings); Player-of-the-Tournament: B. Sachin (Kovai Kings).
